slides.label: Curved Spacetime As Geometry
slides.notes: Open by placing the chapter at the end of the transport act. Earlier chapters taught the metric, curvature, and parallel transport as geometric measuring devices. This lecture asks how those devices become gravity. Keep the opening promise modest: the deck will not derive full relativity, but it will make the object flow visible from metric signature to geodesics, curvature, matter, and the field equation.

slides.label: The Equivalence Principle Has A Curvature Remainder
slides.notes: Use this slide to separate local cancellation from tidal evidence. A freely falling observer can choose a local frame where ordinary gravitational acceleration disappears at a point. That does not make gravity a coordinate illusion. Neighboring falling particles still accelerate relative to one another, and that relative acceleration is what curvature records. This is the first bridge from physical intuition to the geometric language of the course.

slides.label: The Metric Draws Causal Geometry
slides.notes: Make the metric signature concrete before introducing tensors. In Euclidean geometry every nonzero direction has positive squared length. In spacetime the Lorentzian sign split partitions tangent directions into timelike, null, and spacelike. The light cone is not just a drawing of light. It is the metric's local sorting rule for possible causal motion, and changing coordinates must preserve that sorting.

slides.label: Free Fall Means Geodesic Motion
slides.notes: Now translate force language into geometry. A free particle follows a worldline whose tangent vector is transported along itself. In coordinates this becomes the geodesic equation, where the Christoffel symbols express how the coordinate grid itself changes. Emphasize that this is the same transport idea used earlier, but the path now lives in spacetime rather than on a two-dimensional surface.

slides.label: Tidal Stretching Reads The Riemann Tensor
slides.notes: The local figure provides the physical diagnostic. The ellipsoid is a bundle of nearby free-fall trajectories. If all points had the same acceleration, the bundle would translate without deforming. Stretching and squeezing mean neighboring geodesics have different relative accelerations. The geodesic deviation equation is the compact geometric statement: curvature acts on the separation vector and the velocity of the reference worldline.

slides.label: Stress-Energy Is The Source Ledger
slides.notes: Introduce stress-energy as the bookkeeping tensor for matter and radiation, not as a mysterious add-on. Its components record energy density, momentum density, energy flux, and pressure or shear stress. This matters because general relativity does not let mass alone source gravity. The geometry responds to the full local flow of energy and momentum through spacetime.

slides.label: Einstein's Equation Matches Two Tensors
slides.notes: This is the central synthesis slide. The left side is a divergence-free curvature summary built from the metric and its derivatives. The right side is the stress-energy ledger scaled by constants. The equation says that spacetime geometry and physical content must be compared tensor to tensor, so every observer agrees about the geometric relation even when the component table changes.

slides.label: Schwarzschild Geometry Is A Vacuum Test Case
slides.notes: Use Schwarzschild as the first named solution rather than as a computational burden. Outside a spherical nonrotating mass the stress-energy tensor is zero, yet curvature remains because the boundary conditions encode the central mass. The metric coefficient marks the horizon in these coordinates, and free-fall worldlines bend inside the causal structure drawn by the light cones.

slides.label: Classical Tests Become Curvature Effects
slides.notes: This slide turns the equation into observational consequences. Mercury's perihelion shift, light bending, gravitational redshift, and orbital timing are not separate tricks. They are different probes of the same curved metric. The goal is for students to see tests as inspections of geodesics and clocks, not as disconnected historical facts.

slides.label: The Chapter's Geometric Contract
slides.notes: Close by returning to the notebook contract. Each concept is tied to an object, a visual, a formula, and a saved check. Students should leave with one clean chain: matter and radiation determine the metric through the field equation, the metric determines light cones and geodesics, and curvature reveals itself through tidal deviation, waves, horizons, and cosmological expansion.
